title: DeepTIL links invasive-margin lymphocyte density with colorectal cancer progression
summary: DeepTIL used ResNet18 tumor and lymphocyte detectors to quantify immune-cell distributions in colorectal pathology slides. Lymphocyte density within 200 micrometres of the invasive margin remained associated with progression-free survival after adjustment in 180 Yonsei patients and 268 TCGA patients. This retrospective association does not establish clinical benefit; wide confidence intervals, model selection and the outcome-optimized cutpoint limit inference.
organization: Dalian University of Technology; Yonsei University College of Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary full paper Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata;reviewed 2026-11-21.

evidence.tested: Retrospective prognostic analysis in Yonsei 180 and TCGA 268; adjusted associations replicated within the same study.
evidence.unknown: Prospective utility, independent-team replication and causal benefit were not established.
evidence.ai_role: DeepTIL ResNet18 tumor/TIL detectors quantify spatial TIL density; 200micrometre invasive-margin feature associates with progression-free survival in Yonsei180 and retrospective TCGA268.
